MARKE.|103}}</noinclude>he blessed, and brake the loaues, and gaue to his Disciples to set before them: and the tvvo fishes he deuided to al. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=42}}† And al did eate, and had their fill. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=43}}† And they tooke vp the leauings, tvvelue ful baskets of fragments: and of the fishes. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=44}}† And they that did eate, vvere fiue thousand men. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=45}}† And immediatly he compelled his Disciples to goe vp into the boate, that they might goe before him beyond the {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The narrow sea, or water.}}∷ straite to Bethsaida: vvhiles him self did dimisse the people.

{{verse|chapter=6|verse=46}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 14, 23. Io. 6, 16.''}}* And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel on Saterday after Ashwenesday.}}vvhen he had dimissed them, he vvent into the mountaine to pray. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=47}}† And vvhen it vvas late, the boate vvas in the middes of the sea, and him self alone on the land. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=48}}† And seeing them labouring in rovving (for the vvinde vvas against them) and about the fourth vvatch of the night he commeth to them vvalking vpon the sea: and he vvould haue passed by them. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=49}}† But they seeing him vvalking vpon the sea, thought it vvas a ghost, and cried out. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=50}}† For al savv him, and vvere troubled. And immediatly he talked vvith them, and said to them, Haue confidence, it is I, feare ye not. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=51}}† And he vvent vp to them into the shippe, and the vvinde ceased: and they vvere farre more astonied vvithin them selues: {{verse|chapter=6|verse=52}}† for they vnderstoode not concerning the loaues: for their hart vvas blinded.

{{verse|chapter=6|verse=53}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 14, 34.''}}* vvhen they had passed ouer, they came into the land of Genezareth, and set to the shore. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=54}}† And vvhen they vvere gone out of the boate, incontinent they knevv him: {{verse|chapter=6|verse=55}}† and running through that vvhole countrie, they began to carie about in couches those that vvere il at ease, vvhere they heard he vvas. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=56}}† And vvhithersoeuer he entred into tovvnes or into villages or cities, they laid the sicke in the streates, and besought him that they might touche but the hemme of his garment: and as many as touched him, vvere made vvhole.⊣

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. VI.}}}}

''3. The carpenter.'') As his countrie-folkes seeing him not only to be a poore man, but also knowing (as they thought) his vvhole parentage to be but vulgar, not reaching to his Godhead and diuine generation, did take offence or scandal of him: so doe the Heretikes take like offence at his person in the B. Sacrament, saying, Why, this is not God: for it is bread made of corne by such a baker, of the same moulde that such a lofe is: not marking that it was not made Christ by baking, but by Consecration, and the vertue of Christs vvordes.<noinclude>{{continues|''3. They''}}</noinclude>
